title: Echo Agent
description: Use this when you need a reference agent to verify tool-calling wiring or test an orchestrator's delegation path — echoes text verbatim via echo_text or round-trips a JSON payload via echo_json.

title: Memory Organizer
description: Use this when memoryd needs to promote raw episodes into structured graph knowledge — runs batched relation extraction, importance scoring (1–10), contradiction detection, and reflection synthesis via LLM. Invoked by memoryd on the write path; never called on the read path.

title: sox-memory (graph memory subsystem)
description: Use this when you want the full sox-memory graph-memory subsystem installed in one command — expands to memory-server (7 MCP tools, SQLite graph store), memory-organizer (LLM organizer agent), memory-flush (SessionEnd hook), and memory-cli (store lifecycle commands).

title: Memory CLI
description: Use this when you need to manage the sox-memory store from the shell — provides memory init|status|list|registry subcommands for store lifecycle, scope selection, and registry inspection. Fully deterministic; zero LLM calls.

title: Status Command
description: Use this when you want a quick snapshot of the runtime environment — reports node version, cwd, and platform via /status-command without making any LLM calls.

title: Audit Hook
description: Use this when you need an append-only audit trail of every tool invocation — binds PreToolUse and writes one JSON line per call to $AUDIT_HOOK_LOG (default: ~/.sox/audit-hook.log). Deterministic; zero LLM calls.

title: Memory Session Flush
description: Use this when you need session memory durably persisted at conversation end and scope promotions reviewed — binds SessionEnd (persists working memory, enqueues episodes, nudges memoryd) and ScopePromotionProposed (runs promotion approval policy). Deterministic; zero LLM calls.

title: Hello Server
description: Use this when you need a minimal MCP server reference to verify stdio JSON-RPC wiring or template a new tool — exposes one stub tool (example_tool) over a stdio transport.

title: Agent Memory Server
description: Use this when an agent needs durable, searchable memory across sessions — exposes 7 memory_* tools over a single-file SQLite graph store with hybrid recall (vec+BM25+temporal, <50ms, zero LLM), write-enqueue, session state, community lookup, and bi-temporal invalidation.

title: Greeting Prompt
description: Use this when you need to generate a warm, context-aware greeting addressed to a named person — accepts {{name}} (required) and {{context}} (optional) to adjust formality and tone.

title: Hello World
description: Use this when you need a minimal working skill to verify the extension scaffold or test a new host integration — processes a text input and returns it prefixed with 'Processed:'.
